segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin describe the cream as moisturizing without feeling greasy, though a few note mild flaking or dryness during the first days of use.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers most often report no burning or peeling from this retinaldehyde formula, though some advise easing in slowly or limiting use to a few times a week.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin give mixed reports, ranging from significant dryness and peeling in the T-zone to smooth results with no irritation.

concerns.aging: Reviewers report smoother texture and firmer-looking skin, with softened fine lines noticeable after several weeks of use; some say results are subtle or not yet visible after a month.
concerns.dehydration: Some reviewers experience dryness, tightness, or flaking, especially in the first days or with more frequent use, while others report no dryness and describe the cream as hydrating.
concerns.redness: Most reviewers, including several with sensitive skin, report no redness or irritation from this retinaldehyde formula, though a couple mention initial tingling or discomfort.

I've been using the Avène Retrinal 0.05 for about a month and I really like it. I have sensitive skin and most retinoids irritate me, but this one hasn't caused burning or peeling. It's creamy, easy to apply, and layers well with moisturizer. Results are subtle but noticeable — my skin looks smoother and more even, and I've had less dullness overall. It's not a dramatic overnight product, but it feels effective without being harsh. Pricey, but worth it if you want a gentle retinoid you can actually stick with.
